summary: CJ Block emerges as the top candidate for the sweets-first QSR format in Kolkata, driven primarily by its exceptional residential population and food cluster whitespace scores. CL Block follows closely, benefiting from a strong residential population and transit proximity, but suffers from lower scores in affinity points and commercial visibility. AL Block ranks the lowest due to its lack of visibility, delivery catchment density, and transit proximity, despite a decent residential population score.
methodology:
H3 hexagonal grid at resolution 9 (185 cells) over the study area. 8 weighted layers scored per hex with percentile normalization; weighted-sum composite (weights preserved from spec). Walk/drive layers (Residential Population, Affinity POIs - Temples/Markets, Delivery Catchment Density, Transit Proximity, Daytime Generators) scored with calibrated Euclidean proxies (isochrone refinement unavailable).
